subdivision.heading: Additional Rules Specific to Originating Applications for Judicial Review

operative_text.controlling:
3.21   On an originating application for judicial review, no person
may be questioned as a witness for the purpose of obtaining a
transcript for use at the hearing without the Court’s permission.

carrier_notes.BOOK_C: *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.21 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

BOOK_A.title: Limit on Questioning
BOOK_A.commentary:
Presumably R.3.21 is read as if there were a comma after"at the hearing". Judicial review is conducted on the existing record, and allowing discovery or oral evidence is exceptional.

*Evidence on Judicial Review*

BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.3-61 (line 1621) to p.3-62 (line 1633): rule text, Defined Terms 'Court' (the Appendix defines 'Court', line 40688), Related Provisions and a short note; the built commentary (213 characters) is the note's last part and ends with the title of 3.22 ('Evidence on Judicial Review', line 1635); the first part of the note (from 'witness under R.3.21 can be asked ...') is in the rule-text field, kept verbatim in the text note. (1) Related Provisions '6.8 (questioning of a witness before hearing)': official 6.8 is titled 'Questioning witness before hearing' (paraphrase, same subject). (2) 'Presumably R.3.21 is read as if there were a comma after "at the hearing"' is Book A's reading; the official text has no comma ('for use at the hearing without the Court's permission'). (3) 'Judicial review is conducted on the existing record, and allowing discovery or oral evidence is exceptional' agrees in substance with Book C's commentary ('since the record, by the time the matter reaches a judicial review, is established. Presumptively, no additional evidence should be considered'). (4) Pointers: 'See also R.3.22n., infra' and 'See Apotex v. R., R.3.22n., infra' land (the full citation Apotex v. R. 2006 ABCA 133, 384 AR 88, leave den (SCC 12 Oct '06) is in the 3.22 note, p.3-64, line 1689); the pieces before this rule's title on p.3-61 (lines 1617-1621) belong to 3.20's note. (5) Book A's other references to this rule agree with its title and subject: 3.13(2) text '[Limit on questioning]' and related provision '3.21 (questioning on judicial review)' (p.3-31, lines 712 and 715) and 3.22(b) '[Limit on questioning]' (p.3-62, line 1636); this settles the point noted in the 3.13 pass that the label covers judicial review only. (6) Statements of law and the cases (Robertson (#9) 2004 ABQB 243, 355 AR 281 - the same neutral citation and AR citation as in Book B's 3.19 commentary; Bergman 2020 ABQB 661; the Métis Nation case 2021 ABQB 282, printed 'M?tis') were not checked.
